handbookNote: Louisiana Real Estate Broker license exam. Part of the 2026-09-02 R26 population-tier broker buildout. Exam vendor: Pearson VUE, under contract with the Louisiana Real Estate Commission (LREC). PRIMARY-CONFIRMED by directly downloading and reading Pearson VUE's own official Louisiana Real Estate Commission and Louisiana Appraisers Board Candidate Handbook (#091900, July 2024 edition, national content outline effective April 1, 2025, state outline effective September 1, 2021). Exam mechanics: Combo exam = 135 items (80 national + 55 state), 240 minutes, passing score a scaled 75 on each portion (national and state graded/passed independently, same as AL/WI's Pearson VUE structure). track_registry models this as exam_question_count=135, exam_duration_sec=14400, pass_percent=75, min_correct=101 (135 x 0.75 rounded). Broker eligibility: 4 years of active licensure (2 of the 4 immediately preceding application) plus 150 classroom hours including a mandatory 30-hour Broker Responsibilities course (Real Estate 203). NATIONAL PORTION (80 items, Pearson VUE's standard 8-section template, reused verbatim across every state Pearson VUE administers -- confirmed identical in structure, though not identical in item-weights, to AL's and WI's national outlines): I. Real Property Characteristics, Legal Descriptions & Property Use (10), II. Forms of Ownership, Transfer & Recording of Title (8), III. Property Value and Appraisal (10), IV. Real Estate Contracts and Agency (15), V. Real Estate Practice (12), VI. Property Disclosures and Environmental Issues (9), VII. Financing and Settlement (8), VIII. Real Estate Math Calculations (8). LOUISIANA STATE PORTION (55 items, per the official outline effective Sept 2021): I. Duties/Powers of the Real Estate Commission (4-6), II. Licensing Requirements (7-9), III. Statutory Requirements Governing Licensee Activities (13-15 -- advertising, broker/salesperson relationship, commissions, disclosures, conflict of interest, handling of documents/monies, listings, offers, place of business, recordkeeping, property management), IV. Louisiana Civil Law System (13-15, the single largest state-portion section), V. Louisiana Law of Agency (13-15). Section IV was completely missed in the initial 5-topic state drafting pass and added as a same-day gap-fill once the real official outline was fetched -- Louisiana is the ONLY U.S. state using a civil-law property system (movables/immovables, servitudes, usufruct, successions, redhibition, 'privileges' instead of liens, reconduction) rather than English common law, and this gap-fill topic (68 questions, the largest single bucket in this bank) is grounded in ~55 distinct Louisiana Civil Code and Code of Civil Procedure articles read directly from legis.la.gov. Sourced against Louisiana Revised Statutes Title 37 Chapter 17 (La. R.S. 37:1430 et seq., the Real Estate License Law -- note the task brief that initiated this build incorrectly assumed 'Chapter 25'; drafting agents caught this and cited only verified section numbers, never the wrong chapter number) via legis.la.gov, and La. R.S. 9:3891-3898 (Agency Relations in Real Estate Transactions) plus La. R.S. 9:3196-3200 (Residential Property Disclosure) via FindLaw/Justia mirrors of the same statutes, cross-checked against LREC's own site (lrec.gov). A handful of Revised Statutes sub-facts (the Louisiana Condominium Act, Bond for Deed law, usury ceiling, and residential security-deposit statute) could not be independently pinned to a verified citation this session -- legis.la.gov's Revised Statutes table of contents is a JS-postback tree that resisted automated navigation -- and were deliberately omitted rather than guessed; a future backfill pass could close this small gap. This bank was drafted across 14 parallel single-topic drafting passes (8 national + 6 state-law categories including the Civil Law gap-fill), each instructed to draft as many genuinely distinct, real, grounded questions as its topic's source material supports with NO target number or ceiling. Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_broker_answers.js, producing a final near-even 25.0/25.0/25.0/24.9% A/B/C/D distribution. 551 raw questions drafted against a 135-item exam -- a 4.08:1 pool ratio. This clears the standing 4:1 new-track floor but sits below the preferred 5:1 target; a future backfill pass (most naturally targeting the Civil Law and Contracts/Agency sections, which carry the largest real item weights) would be worth prioritizing before this track is treated as fully depth-hardened.
